stem: At the end of Chapter I, what is Gatsby reaching toward across the water?
choices: A green light at the end of a dock
A lighthouse on a rocky point
A lit window in Tom's house
A boat sailing across the bay

evidence.quote: a single green light, minute and far away, that might have been the end of a dock

explanation: Nick later learns the light is at the end of Daisy's dock. It comes to stand for everything Gatsby is reaching for.

stem: Nick says Tom has "a rather hard mouth and a supercilious manner." What does supercilious mean?
choices: Acting superior to others
Shy and quick to blush
Kind and very patient
Easily confused by others

evidence.quote: a rather hard mouth and a supercilious manner. Two shining arrogant eyes had established dominance over his face

explanation: The next sentence calls his eyes 'arrogant' and says they show 'dominance.' Supercilious means looking down on others.

stem: Daisy hopes her daughter will be "a beautiful little fool." What does this show about Daisy?
choices: She thinks women are better off not knowing much
She is proud her daughter is so clever
She wants her daughter to become famous
She thinks her daughter is unkind

evidence.quote: that’s the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool

explanation: Daisy says everything is 'terrible anyhow.' She seems to believe a woman in her world is happiest if she doesn't see it clearly.

stem: What watches over the valley of ashes from a billboard?
choices: The eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg
A painted statue of a soldier
A picture of Gatsby's mansion
The face of a smiling movie star

evidence.quote: above the grey land and the spasms of bleak dust which drift endlessly over it, you perceive, after a moment, the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg

explanation: The faded eyes of an old eye-doctor's ad look out over the ashes, like someone watching everything that happens.

stem: A guest in Gatsby's library is amazed the books are "absolutely real—have pages and everything." Why does this matter?
choices: Gatsby's world feels like a stage set, so real things surprise
Gatsby is a scholar who reads every book
The guest is planning to steal the books
Books were rare and costly in the 1920s

evidence.quote: “Absolutely real—have pages and everything. I thought they’d be a nice durable cardboard.”

explanation: He expected props. Even the man who admires the books assumes Gatsby's life is a performance.

stem: Who does Gatsby say "fixed the World's Series back in 1919"?
choices: Meyer Wolfshiem
Tom Buchanan
George Wilson
Jordan Baker

evidence.quote: “He’s the man who fixed the World’s Series back in 1919.”

explanation: Gatsby's business partner is a gambler and a criminal, a hint about where Gatsby's money comes from.

stem: According to Jordan, why did Gatsby buy his house in West Egg?
choices: So Daisy would be just across the bay
It was the biggest house on Long Island
To be close to Wolfshiem's business
Because Nick lived right next door

evidence.quote: “Gatsby bought that house so that Daisy would be just across the bay.”

explanation: The house, the parties, and the green light all point to one goal: Daisy.

stem: Daisy cries into Gatsby's shirts and says she's "never seen such—such beautiful shirts before." What is she really upset about?
choices: The life she could have had with Gatsby
She dislikes the colors of the shirts
She is jealous of all of Gatsby's money
She is tired from the long drive over

evidence.quote: “It makes me sad because I’ve never seen such—such beautiful shirts before.”

explanation: The shirts stand for the wealth Gatsby built to win her. Seeing it all at once, five years too late, overwhelms her.

choices: James Gatz
Jay Gordon
Jim Gatsworth
James Gates

evidence.quote: James Gatz—that was really, or at least legally, his name.

explanation: James Gatz of North Dakota invented 'Jay Gatsby' at seventeen.

stem: Nick tells Gatsby, "You can't repeat the past." What does Gatsby's answer show?
choices: He believes he can win Daisy back as before
He agrees the past is gone for good
He wants to forget about Daisy
He plans to move back home west

evidence.quote: “Can’t repeat the past?” he cried incredulously. “Why of course you can!”

explanation: Gatsby wants Daisy to say she never loved Tom, as if the last five years could be erased.

stem: Gatsby says Daisy's "voice is full of money." What does he mean?
choices: Her charm is bound up with wealth and status
She talks about money all of the time
She has a loud and ringing voice
She owes many people a lot of money

evidence.quote: “Her voice is full of money,” he said suddenly.

explanation: Nick realizes this is 'the inexhaustible charm' of her voice. Part of what Gatsby loves in Daisy is the world of money she belongs to.

stem: Who was driving Gatsby's car when it struck Myrtle Wilson?
choices: Daisy
Gatsby
Tom
Jordan

evidence.quote: “Was Daisy driving?” “Yes,” he said after a moment, “but of course I’ll say I was.”

explanation: Gatsby tells Nick that Daisy was driving, and that he'll take the blame for her.

stem: How did George Wilson find his way to Gatsby?
choices: Tom told him who owned the car
Daisy sent him to Gatsby's house
Wolfshiem paid him to go there
He saw Gatsby driving that day

evidence.quote: He was crazy enough to kill me if I hadn’t told him who owned the car.

explanation: Tom admits to Nick that he told Wilson the yellow car was Gatsby's, sending Wilson after him.

stem: The novel ends: "So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past." What does this suggest?
choices: People push forward but the past keeps pulling them back
Rowing is the best way to cross the bay
Nick has decided to become a sailor
The future is always easy to reach

evidence.quote: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.

explanation: Like Gatsby, everyone keeps reaching for something ahead while being dragged back by what has already happened.

stem: Put these events in the order they happen.

events.text: Nick sees Gatsby reaching toward a green light

evidence.quote: a single green light, minute and far away, that might have been the end of a dock

events.text: A guest finds Gatsby's books are real

evidence.quote: It makes me sad because I’ve never seen such—such beautiful shirts before.
“Was Daisy driving?” “Yes,” he said after a moment

explanation: Gatsby's longing, his show of wealth, the reunion, and the crash that ends it.
